title: Normalized whole-tower comparison of the two integral pullbacks
statement:
Fix a finite-field datum $(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], a prime $\ell\ne p$, and an algebraic closure $\Omega/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $T$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible, in the sense of [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]; such schemes are called allowed. For each finite $E\subset\Omega$ over $\mathbf Q_\ell$, use the framework integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^s(T)$ of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] and the PBC integral category and raw rationalization $\mathcal C_E^p(T)$ of [def-weil-pbc-rational-category].
For every scheme $W$ satisfying the same hypotheses, suppose $I_{W,E}$ is the integral identity equivalence and $J_{W,E}$ its exact raw rationalization, with the identity formulas on integral objects and tensor morphisms. Use the specified completion inverses $j_{W,L/E}=\chi_{L/E}^{-1}[1/\varpi_L]$ and the normalized framework scalar associators of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Write $F^s_{h,E}$ and $F^p_{h,E}$ for the actual integral completed pullbacks of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback]. For all scheme isomorphisms $h:U\xrightarrow{\sim}T$ between allowed schemes, simultaneously for all finite $E$, there are natural integral isomorphisms
$$b^{\mathrm{int}}_{h,E}:I_{U,E}F^s_{h,E}\xrightarrow{\sim}F^p_{h,E}I_{T,E}.$$
On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$ of $K$ they are the realization of the identity on the entire strict tower
$$Q_{h,E}(P)_n=\operatorname{Res}_n h_n^*(P\otimes_{R_{E,T}}(\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n)_T),$$
with its actual quotient transitions. The product-cone and K-injective-derived-limit realizations are identified by the natural Roos map $\lim I_\bullet\to\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_I)[-1]$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$, for a tower K-injective replacement $Q\to I$. This comparison is independent of representatives and resolutions and restricts to the integral constructible categories. Its inverse, ambient lift and raw rationalization give the finite datum of [def-fd-finite-pullback-comparison-datum], including its actual unit-section chain map and zero shifted coordinate.
These choices are simultaneous with a whole-diagram realization system of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. For identity maps the unit equation is
$$u^p I\circ b^{\mathrm{int}}_{1}=Iu^s.$$
For $h:U\simeq V$, $k:V\simeq T$, with the specified comparisons $c^s,c^p:F_{kh}\to F_hF_k$, the equation is
$$c^p I\circ b^{\mathrm{int}}_{kh}=(F_h^p b^{\mathrm{int}}_k)\circ(b^{\mathrm{int}}_h F_k^s)\circ(Ic^s).$$
The source comparisons are exactly the whole-tower counit-normalized ones and the target comparisons are the actual PBC ones. For scalar change let $\alpha^s:S_UF^s_{h,E}\to F^s_{h,L}S_T$ and $\alpha^p:P_UF^p_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,L}P_T$ be the specified comparisons, now rationalized, and write $b_{h,E}$ for the rationalization of $b^{\mathrm{int}}_{h,E}$. Then
$$F^p_{h,L}(j_T)\circ b_{h,L,S_TK}\circ J_{U,L}(\alpha^s_K)=\alpha^p_{J_{T,E}K}\circ P_U(b_{h,E,K})\circ j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}.$$
The corresponding integral equation uses the specified completion maps. All these equations respect shifts, repeated fields, successive coefficient extension and arbitrary finite scheme compositions, as equalities of whole quotient diagrams before realization, with their tower counits retained.

proof.text: Identify both integral coefficient sheaves with $R_{E,W}=\lim_n(A_{E,n})_W$ and their full constructible subcategories using [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. For an isomorphism $h$, [lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image] identifies inverse image with reindexing the pro-etale site, an exact equivalence preserving limits. Applying this to the coefficient limit gives $h^{-1}R_{E,T}\simeq R_{E,U}$ with precisely its quotient-defined structure map. By [lem-weil-sheaf-scalar-extension-ring-iso], module pullback is this same exact inverse image with transported action. It is exact on strict towers as well, since exactness is levelwise. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization] computes its tower-derived functor by the termwise functor itself. On the reductions of any flat-term K-flat $P$, the two constructions in [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] therefore have the identical strict tower $Q_{h,E}(P)$, including every quotient arrow. This argument does not require the quotient complexes to be K-flat over the completed ring.

source.place: Final sentence: identifying the completed coefficient and finite pullback presentations; Stacks 099N, proetale.tex, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5).

proof.text:
Put $H(Q)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s_Q)[-1]$. Countable products of $R_{E,U}$-modules are exact by [lem-weil-proetale-countable-products-exact], so [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] applies to the common strict tower, not merely to its evaluations in a triangulated category. For a K-injective tower replacement $q:Q\to I$, write $\iota_I:\lim I\to H(I)$, $z\mapsto(0,z)$. Define the ambient comparison by
$$b^{\mathrm{amb}}_{h,E,P}=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]:H(Q)\xrightarrow{\sim}\lim I.$$
Insert on each side the defining realization identifications from Step 1. This is the requested direction $IF^s_h\to F^p_hI$ and is the realization comparison of the identity morphism of $Q$. The cited lemma asserts both that these arrows are invertible and that the resulting comparison is natural for morphisms of entire derived towers.

source.place: Tag 0941, lemma-derived-limit-is-ok, proof; normalized exact-product Roos comparison refinement.

proof.text: The K-flat representative comparisons in [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined] carry strict quotient maps to strict quotient maps and are compatible with the defining localized functors. Naturality and resolution independence of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] therefore identify the preceding $b$ for every change of $P$, $q$, or common refinement. The uniqueness of descent of natural transformations in [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] extends these identities from representative maps to all derived morphisms. Hence $b^{\mathrm{amb}}$ is a natural isomorphism on the ambient categories. Framework pullback preserves the integral constructible category by [lem-pur-integral-operations-preserve-constructible]; the isomorphic PBC object is in the same full category by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-stratified-perfect-characterization]. Restrict $b^{\mathrm{amb}}$ to obtain $b^{\mathrm{int}}$.

source.place: Final sentence: independence of representatives and restriction to the common full integral category.

proof.text:
For the ordinary module pullback $G_hP$, let $\gamma_n:G_hP\to Q_{h,E}(P)_n$ be the finite quotient augmentation. On an inverse-image unit section it sends $\gamma_h(p)$ to $\gamma_h(p\otimes1)\otimes1$. Thus it is exactly finite reduction followed by finite inverse-image unit. The quotient transitions give $t_n\gamma_{n+1}=\gamma_n$ as chain maps, so
$$\Gamma_P:G_hP\to H(Q),\qquad x\mapsto(0,(\gamma_nx)_n)$$
is a chain map: the shifted differential term is $-(1-s)(\gamma_nx)_n=0$. The augmentation clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] gives $b^{\mathrm{amb}}\Gamma_P=v^p_P$, the canonical derived-limit augmentation. By [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] this is its actual completion map, with the ordinary derived-pullback counit inserted. The constant-tower identification is normalized by the universal counit equation of [lem-cbc-derived-constant-tower-normalization]; no arbitrary cone filler is involved. Multiplying this equality by $(b^{\mathrm{amb}})^{-1}$ gives precisely the ambient localization/counit equation required by [def-fd-finite-pullback-comparison-datum]. Its integral datum is $(b^{\mathrm{int}})^{-1}$, and its rational datum is the localization of this inverse. The formula for $\Gamma_P$ supplies the required chain lift and its zero shifted coordinate.

source.place: Final sentence: actual unit-section chain map and finite pullback comparison datum.

proof.text: Choose once the simultaneous realization system asserted by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. On each common quotient tower use the natural comparison of Step 2. Its augmentation normalization identifies the constant-tower/derived-limit counit on a K-injective model with $\Delta\lim I\to I$, since both maps are the same compatible limit cone before localization. Consequently its derived-change-of-rings adjunct on whole quotient systems is the same whole-system counit. The substitution statement [lem-trf-counit-realization-substitution] now identifies every iterated framework realization with realization of the corresponding word of system operations, retaining that counit at each intermediate object. All these intermediate objects are constructible and complete by the stated domain assertions of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization]. Naturality of Step 2 is on the entire tower category, so this single family works for all representatives, maps and finite coefficient fields simultaneously.

source.place: Final sentence: simultaneous choices with the fixed whole-diagram realization system.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], every ideal of $\mathcal O_E$ is principal, hence finitely generated, so this coefficient ring is Noetherian. Transport the constant-coefficient completed adjunction through [lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence], which identifies the finite reduction towers, derived limits and completion units with those for the completed ring sheaf. We verify that the PBC composition normalization is the actual one. By [lem-sp-completed-pullback-adjunction], its adjunction is induced by ordinary pullback/direct image and the completion adjunction, with the indicated hom-set bijections. The conjugation bijection of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] defines its compositor from direct-image composition. Under those hom-set bijections its precomposition with the completion units is ordinary pullback composition: the inserted unit and counit cancel by the adjunction triangle identities. On a representative this ordinary map is the termwise $c_{h,k,n}$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. This identifies the PBC map uniquely: for an isomorphism the ordinary inverse image of a complete object is already complete, as witnessed by the invertible specified unit in [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], and the PBC unit is the same invertible augmentation by Steps 2 and 4. Thus precomposition with that unit is injective on Hom. This argument checks equality of completed maps by an invertible unit, rather than by separate finite evaluations.

source.place: Tag 099N, lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case (2),(5); actual completed-adjunction normalization and Tag 0D6D, sites-cohomology.tex, lemma-derived-pullback-composition.

proof.text:
Here is the composition equation explicitly. Suppress the identity $I$ and coefficient index, put $\kappa^s_h:G_h\to F^s_h$ for the augmentation of Step 4 and $\kappa^p_h=b_h\kappa^s_h$, and let $c^G:G_{kh}\to G_hG_k$ be ordinary composition. Step 5 and the source normalization give
$$c^s\kappa^s_{kh}=(F^s_h\kappa^s_k)(\kappa^s_hG_k)c^G.$$
Step 6 gives the identical formula with $s$ replaced by $p$. Substitute $\kappa^p=b\kappa^s$ in the latter formula and use naturality of $b_h$ at $\kappa^s_k$. Both sides of
$$c^p b_{kh}=(F^p_h b_k)(b_hF^s_k)c^s$$
then have the same composite with $\kappa^s_{kh}$. This is invertible by [lem-weil-isomorphism-derived-pullback-comparison-normalization], so cancel it. For identity maps the same calculation reads $u^p b_1\kappa^s_1=u^s\kappa^s_1$, giving $u^p b_1=u^s$. Reinsert $I$ to obtain exactly the two displayed integral equations. The source $c^s$ used here is the whole-system counit formula fixed by [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization].

source.place: Final sentence: unit and composition equations, with their explicit cancellation argument.

proof.text:
For scalar change write $C_W=-\otimes^L_{R_{E,W}}R_{L,W}$ for ordinary PBC extension and $S_W$ for framework extension. The coefficient sheaf $R_{L,W}$ is finite free over $R_{E,W}$, and $\chi_W:C_W\to S_W$ is the specified quotient/zero-coordinate completion map, by [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison]. Use the actual strict tower map $d_\bullet$ in [lem-weil-specified-pullback-comparison-alpha]; it is specified on both cone coordinates and on all quotient transitions, and defines $\delta^s:C_UF^s_{h,E}\to F^s_{h,L}C_T$. That lemma gives
$$\alpha^s=F^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\,\delta^s\,\chi_{U,F^s_{h,E}}^{-1}.$$
On the PBC realization use the derived limit of the same entire $d_\bullet$, together with tensor/limit comparison, to obtain $\delta^p:C_UF^p_{h,E}\to F^p_{h,L}C_T$. This is the specified $\alpha^p$: the ordinary scalar mate is the balanced tensor map by [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization], and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-strict-tower-transport] identifies its derived-limit and augmented-tower realizations. These are the canonical integral change-of-rings/completed-pullback comparisons of [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]. This identification retains the completion unit; no level map $d_n$ is asserted to be invertible. The framework scalar comparison $a_h=\mu_h^{-1}\lambda_h$ of [lem-trf-integral-pullback-comparison-realization], used in Steps 5 and 11, is this same $\alpha^s$: $\lambda_h\chi_U$ and $\mu_hF^s_{h,L}(\chi_T)\delta^s$ are both the derived maps induced by the strict augmentation of $C_UF^s_{h,E}K$ by its unshifted level-$m$ projection followed by $d_m$, so they agree by the augmentation clause of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison].

source.place: Final sentence: comparing the specified framework and actual PBC scalar/pullback maps.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-cbc-exact-product-functor-roos-descent] to the exact tensor functor $C_U$; its product and limit comparisons are the canonical ones from [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-strict-tower-transport]. Its hypotheses on normalized Roos comparisons hold by Step 2, and finite freeness gives the required product preservation. That lemma identifies tensor transport of $\rho_Q=[\iota_I]^{-1}[H(q)]$ with the PBC derived-limit transport, with the universal units retained. Naturality of [lem-weil-strict-roos-comparison] for the whole tower morphism $d_\bullet$ therefore gives
$$b_{h,L,C_TK}\,\delta^s_K=\delta^p_{IK}\,C_U(b_{h,E,K}).$$
This is an equality of the realized whole-diagram maps with their fixed model identifications. In particular the argument includes the transition maps and the derived-limit counit, not just their images at each finite quotient.

source.place: Final sentence: whole-tower naturality under finite-free coefficient transport.

proof.text:
Substitute the formula for $\alpha^s$ of Step 8 and the equality of Step 9. Naturality of $b_{h,L}$ at $\chi_T$ gives
$$F^p_{h,L}(\chi_T^{-1})\,b_{h,L,S_TK}\,\alpha^s_K
=b_{h,L,C_TK}\,\delta^s_K\,\chi_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}^{-1}
=\alpha^p_{IK}\,C_U(b_{h,E,K})\,\chi_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}^{-1}.$$
This is the integral completion-map equation, in the requested direction. The raw localization of [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi] acts on integral morphisms by $f\mapsto f\otimes1$ and preserves composition and inverses. Apply it to this equation and write $j=\chi^{-1}[1/\varpi_L]$. Ordinary $C_U$ rationalizes to $P_U$ by [prop-weil-pbc-scalar-extension]; the resulting equation is exactly
$$F^p_{h,L}(j_T)b_{h,L,S_TK}J_{U,L}(\alpha^s_K)=\alpha^p_{J_{T,E}K}P_U(b_{h,E,K})j_{U,F^s_{h,E}K}.$$
The inverse of the same localized $b$ is the rational part of the finite datum in Step 4.

source.place: Final sentence: integral mixed square and its raw rationalization.

proof.text: For an integer shift $r$, the signed cone comparison $H(Q[r])\to H(Q)[r]$ sends $(y,x)$ to $((-1)^r y,x)$. Its commutation with the cone differential is checked by substituting $d_{Q[r]}=(-1)^r d_Q$. It sends $(0,z)$ to $(0,z)$; hence the defining zigzag for $b$ commutes with shifts, with the canonical exact-functor localization shifts of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. Both coordinates of every scalar cone map are given by the same degree-zero $d_\bullet$, so the same calculation applies to the scalar square. For arbitrary finite words, [lem-trf-quotient-system-mixed-coherence] gives associativity, unit, repeated-field and coefficient-tower equations in entire quotient diagrams. Transport these equations using Step 5 and the normalization checks in Steps 6 and 8. Adjacent model comparisons and their inverses cancel by [lem-trf-counit-realization-substitution]. Thus all the preceding equations are compatible with successive coefficient extensions and any finite scheme composition. The scalar associators are exactly its $\chi$-conjugated tensor associators; repeated fields use its multiplication/completeness unit. Applying raw localization preserves these equalities. This proves every remaining coherence assertion without a finite Tor-amplitude assumption.
